geeklist.title: '25 Dice Tower West Virtual Flea Market
geeklist.description:
[center][b]DTW kicks off March 5th, but why wait to spend money until then? On the flip side, maybe you'll sell a few items ahead of time so you can buy more stuff when you get there![/b]
[IMG]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/41d157_53fc1511dcec4a6b98175ae3a6eb0e37~mv2_d_1372_1474_s_2.gif[/IMG][/center]
[b]What's this list for?[/b]
If you have items you'd like to sell at Dice Tower West, you can list them here. This is not part of the physical flea market that is happening at the con. This is just a forum to work out deals in advance of the con so that you can pack/plan accordingly.
[b]***Scheduled meet-up Friday 10 AM.***[/b] See Location Below
[imageid=8731775 large]
Not everyone will be able to make this. It's recommended that you exchange contact info and touch base with your trade partner(s) before the con.
********************************************************************************
[b]Guidelines[/b]
When you list your item, include the condition of the game and the price you'd like to sell it for. It's up to you to decide how you want the item to be sold (e.g. Fixed price, auction, best offer, etc). The transaction will be handled by you from beginning to end. Don't get offended by offers below your asking price. This is a format where haggling is accepted, if not expected.
Please be aware, that not everyone attends the entire convention. If this is you, it's helpful to list when you will/won't be there to avoid missing your buyer/seller.
[b]Don't be a jerk![/b] By agreeing to buy/sell a game, your partner is counting on you to keep your word. They are losing the chance to buy/sell with another person. Please only agree to a deal if you plan on honoring your word. If life happens and you won't be able to complete your transaction, please send them a direct message asap. Also, there is no need to publicly question prices. The market will dictate the value, it's not up to you to police it:cool:
It's best not to delete sold listings. This is your proof of the agreed price and condition. Just mark them as "sold" or change the photo to one that says "sold". You can change the picture ID to 6602898 & it will display this :arrowS:.
[ImageID=6602898 micro]
[u]Be careful of double-listing 1 game.[/u] If you plan on listing a game here and in the math trade, make sure you don't commit it to 2 people. Remove it from the math trade as soon as you have a deal here, or hold off on listing it until after the trade.
Please do not delete and repost your game or post it to this list more than once in an effort to "bump" to the front of the line. ********************************************************************************
Most transactions will be handled at the con (ie: exchange cash for the game). You are expected to process your transactions in the Marketplace to pay BGG their 3% commission on all sales assisted by this site. The 3% is automatically added to Geek Marketplace transactions.
There are a couple of ways you can capture the items you have sold on the list:
1. List each transaction in the marketplace. There is a quick link to do this under each of your listings. Then, send your buyer the link for the listing.
2. You can also create a marketplace dummy sale item something like "Miscellaneous - DTW VFM Commission" as the item type/description and price it at whatever ends up being your total for sales, then mark it "sold". This will generate a seller's invoice via Geek Mail for the 3% commission payable by PayPal.
3. BGG's commission is on the honor system and will not be policed by me.
******************************************************************************** Amazing tools provided by [user=Carnage994][/user]
Alpha List of Games Offered: https://www.yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/349103 Quick add tool: https://www.yulgame.com/Vfm/AddItems/349103
You can post games you want to buy here: [geeklist=349632][/geeklist]

I know some folks don't love the chaotic format of the official meetup on Friday. Some cons limit the number of participants in order to map out designated locations for each seller to facilitate a smoother handoff, which I am not interested in doing. I also don't want to implement a process that would make things more difficult for a gamer who's there solo.
I am interested in discussing ways to improve the experience. Please post ideas and suggestions below, or send me a DM.

If tables were in the same format as the in person flea market it would give us a pretty good traffic pattern instead of having tables in the format of sitting down and playing games. Having some paper and thick markers for people who forget to make signs might also help.
What "official meetup on Friday"? This is DTW. Are you referring to something from a Year ago and under a different Venue?

[q="Delwayne"]What "official meetup on Friday"? This is DTW. Are you referring to something from a Year ago and under a different Venue?[/q]
The official meetup that will take place on Friday, during DTW.

Having VFM sellers in alphabetical sections or rows by their designated BGG username is SUPER helpful, based upon a number of other convention VFMS that I participate in. Makes it way easier to find people in the allotted timeframe, rather than a hodgepodge of random sellers all over the place. The Cons that I go to have reusable laminated letters of the alphabet taped to the wall/floor/table, depending upon the area setup, with sellers arranged in a horseshoe pattern for traffic flow. If that’s too much work, even just having all of the sellers in certain alphabet ranges in designated areas would help a lot (e.g. all A-D sellers in one row). Thanks for being open to suggestions. 😊

Just wanted to post a few notes:
I would like everyone to take a deep breath and remember that we're just buying and selling games here, there is no reason to let your blood pressure elevate.
I realize it's frustrating when a game is advertised for $X, you state you'll pay $X, and then a higher offer is posted. It is also frustrating when games come along for generous prices and are snapped up instantly, especially if it's a game you had your heart set on. It happens every year. It's a function of excitement, not malice.
For sellers, I recommend including "Or Best Offer". Yes, many read that as "Offers below my asking price", but it also covers situations where someone wants to make an offer over your asking price.
For auctions, please also state when it will end. I realize that auctions are appealing to sellers as they feel like a guarantee that you don't leave any money on the table, but there are MANY of us working with a budget and won't bid on something that ties us part of that budget for 2+ months. Starting Bid + Buy it Now Price + End date is a great recipe for happy buyers & sellers :)

I use FP primarily. I'm not a big fan of negotiating in games or IRL. It mostly means firm price to me but I will occasionally make exceptions so Fixed price might be better. Either way it signifies that it's not an auction and if you offer that price then you get that game, regardless of if someone comes in right after you and offers more. That eliminates the OBO questions as well.

Quick Tip:
If you have several copies of something available, avoid using "sold" in your listing until all copies are spoken for. Otherwise, it will show the listing as sold in the alpha list.
Using "claimed by", "going to", or something along those lines will help you keep track of the sold copies without showing them as unavailable to anyone using the alpha list.

Question: How do you mark a sold item as going to a specific person? I see some people are able to show exactly who bought it in the description text. I cannot see how to do this. Thanks for your help.

[q="Mahugh"]Question: How do you mark a sold item as going to a specific person? I see some people are able to show exactly who bought it in the description text. I cannot see how to do this. Thanks for your help. [/q]
1) Click the little "chain link" icon above the text box. 2) Type (or paste) their username in the search box. 3) Below the search box it defaults to "board game", change that to "user" :)

[q="BentlyCash"][q="Mahugh"]Question: How do you mark a sold item as going to a specific person? I see some people are able to show exactly who bought it in the description text. I cannot see how to do this. Thanks for your help. [/q]
1) Click the little "chain link" icon above the text box. 2) Type (or paste) their username in the search box. 3) Below the search box it defaults to "board game", change that to "user" :)[/q] The other way is to click through the user name to his/her page and copy the URL, for example, “https://boardgamegeek.com/user/BentlyCash”. Then click the chain icon and paste the URL into the “Paste Any Link” box, click Next, then click “Add Link” . The result is [user=BentlyCash][/user]

Some helpful tips for the exchange:
- Have a sign with your username so others can find you! [i]I will try my best to bring some paper and markers for anyone who forgot.[/i] I've seen some really clever solutions, like a shirt with username and avatar, sandwich boards, and posters with all trade partners listed. Also, don't forget most of us know you by your username. - Be organized, a physical list of your trade partners and deals is ideal, rather than scrolling and trying to find all of your deals online. - Be on time, every year 95% of the deals are complete by 10:20, then we spend 40 minutes looking for a small handful of folks. - Have change. The casino ticket redemption ATM's break bills for free, but be prepared to spend $10 on ATM fees if you need cash :(

item.comment: Hi! I’m interested in this item. Not sure of the next step…

Hi, if you decide to purchase this, I can mark it as sold to you. We can meet at the official meetup on Friday, March 7, to complete the exchange, where you’ll pay me, and I’ll give you the game. Alternatively, I’m happy to meet at another time during the convention that week if we arrange it in advance.
Let me know if you have any other questions!

item.comment:
I learned this at last year's con. It's quite a slog to set up and learn from the rulebook and likely turns some people off from the game, myself included.
I decided to give it another try later in the year and I'm glad I did, it's a fantastic mid-heavy weight game. I would be happy to teach and play it with whoever buys it.
I typically bring 1 game to the con and teach it as often as possible. Happy to make this my '25 game if folks are up for a longer game.
That's awesome, Ben. Thanks for the offer!
If you guys need players to play this in the evening, let me know.
I'm scheduled to play this on Sunday evening.

I had totally forgotten that my game was missing some things when I bought it used off of someone else. It was missing the rules; easy enough to print off of here, so I did. It was missing the six start markers to mark the railway systems; I used five of mine from a Ticket to Ride game I had. It seemed like it should also have something to keep track of scores, but there is nothing listed for that so I guess maybe not? But then the rules say to use a locomotive to keep track of the scores. Again, I just used trains from TtR.
Disregard comments below from those who bid on this while I was unintentionally misrepresenting this.

Is there anything different about the promo edition?

[q="lausdower"]Is there anything different about the promo edition?[/q] Single chunky box for a single stack as opposed to a flatter box with two stacks of cards sitting side by side. And it says promo. I believe that's about it

Interesting, I got mine at PAX and it has just the one stack. I also ordered one from barnes and noble for a friend and the box size was the same, though I haven't opened it yet. I see there is also a version that says "promotional version" what is the box size for that one? Is there an insert?

[q="lausdower"]Interesting, I got mine at PAX and it has just the one stack. I also ordered one from barnes and noble for a friend and the box size was the same, though I haven't opened it yet. I see there is also a version that says "promotional version" what is the box size for that one? Is there an insert?[/q]
I'll be honest, I had no idea what the difference is beyond what I've read online. No insert in mine. Just a box of cards
Promo edition indeed comes in a small tuck box. If I'm not mistaken, the card stock is also a bit lesser quality than the retail versions.

[q="Mattintheweb"]Promo edition indeed comes in a small tuck box. If I'm not mistaken, the card stock is also a bit lesser quality than the retail versions.[/q]
The box cardstock is lesser quality or the cards themselves?

[q="lausdower"]The box cardstock is lesser quality or the cards themselves?[/q] Both, actually. I don't think the games were produced by the same manufacturers, and I was not able to compare cards from both versions. However, I must say that I've played plenty of games with my promo edition since I got it at Gen Con, and you couldn't tell just by looking at the cards (the tuck box is another story, though 😅). But I think it is what it says it is: a promo edition.
Perfect game for a large group when at a restaurant, or when your brain is fried from heavier games earlier in the day. 👍🏻

Haha I actually underestimated this game then tried it out with a few groups and it was a major hit + a great way to get non-gamers to the table. Hope you win it!
It's a great game. I got it a PAX and have introduced it to numerous people since.

item.comment:
I just want to drop a quick plug for this game. It’s fantastic for anyone that enjoys the idea of deck building, but hates the random uncertainty. It’s a face up pseudo-tableau building game where you are in complete control of how often your powerful cards come up.
It was originally released in German only and folks used to pay gobs of money to custom print the cards in English. It’s a shame that it took several years for the English edition to come out and the luster had already worn off. Great game at a great price.

item.comment: Was this ever released retail? If so, can you tell me what might be different between the versions? I thought this was a KS only situation.

Hey, both, publisher here: there is no such thing a "KS version". We released what we call a "1st edition". The same "base game" went to backers that was available in stores. Backers did get some add-ons for free, but all of those add-ons were also available for purchase after the campaign. Mark's copy appears to have 2 add-ons: the Board Game Media and Quality Beast Customer packs.
Hope this helps!

24 city tiles (four each of six designs) 40 forest tiles (eight each of five designs) 9 ocean tiles 14 special tiles (the original eleven, plus three new ones)

[q="MBorcher54"][q="cubato"]I’ll just point out that all of his other listings have been fixed price sales.[/q] Didn't stop others on another one of bins[/q]
The situation you’re referring to was unfortunate do to the seller opening up bidding for a listing that what originally listed as an $XX OBO and claimed. People only started bidding after the seller allowed it. But in this current listing people started bidding without any indication it was an auction.

[q="cubato"][q="MBorcher54"][q="cubato"]I’ll just point out that all of his other listings have been fixed price sales.[/q] Didn't stop others on another one of bins[/q]
The situation you’re referring to was unfortunate do to the seller opening up bidding for a listing that what originally listed as an $XX OBO and claimed. People only started bidding after the seller allowed it. But in this current listing people started bidding without any indication it was an auction.[/q]
I still am of the opinion that when someone says, for example, $25 OBO, if someone offers $25 and then someone offers $26, $26 is a better offer and should have no qualms taking $26. Why should a "best offer" have to be below what they originally asked for?
I've always seen OBO used in the sense that the offers are lower. But it looks like things are different in this VFM.

[q="iStillLikeCatan"]I've always seen OBO used in the sense that the offers are lower. But it looks like things are different in this VFM.[/q]
That's how I view OBO as well.

If you search online for what OBO means, i think you’ll find that there’s a general consensus on its meaning. It’s not meant to say “here’s my price I’ll sell it at that price or higher”. It’s more like “ideally I’d like to get x amount, but might take the best (lower than I listed) price that someone offers”.
If you have a minimum price but would want to sell higher, just make it an auction. The YUL game tool has good options for starting bid, fixed price, buy it now. But even then, I’m not sure what’s the difference between fixed price and buy it now.
100% agree with everything Alex just said

In this particular listing, it was not the seller’s fault. He clearly listed the item at $5. But by me commenting with the conditional “…if bin” I then opened it up to interpretation for others. Lesson learned.

It has the PGC logo on the back next to Joyple Games. 2023 version. It is KINGs:Tricktakers for sure.
Also I'm happy to provide photos if you want to see.
That would be great, thank you!

Just to jump in with some clarification. Our logo (the PGC logo) is on the box because of the collaboration/friendship we have with Hiroken and TRICKTAKERs Games (previously Joyple Games). The only "work" that PGC provided on KINGs: TRICKTAKERs was the little bit of rulebook translations I did and the how to play video I made. We do not have any rights to KINGs: TRICKTAKERs and would not truly classify this game as the PGC version. It is the Joyple version. Our logo is just there as a courtesy and kindness from Hiroken. In fact, it was Hiroken's idea to have our logo on the box. We never asked/demanded for it, he wanted it there. (He is an awesome and very sweet guy if that wasn't clear 😅)
Same reason applies to the TRICKTAKERs Games version of Eternal Decks. Our logo is on it because I provided a lot of help on it, but it is technically his published game.
Anyway, I think the bigger question might be to ask is whether this is the standard (includes all the wooden cookies tokens and special cards) or compact edition of the game. [i]Note: This is a clarification question for those looking at the post, I am not looking to buy the game...I have a copy![/i]
Ah, thank you so much for clarifying Ryan!
Thank you Ryan for that info. Daniel, I've send you a DM with a photo.
Thanks for the photo and patience 🙂 I'll take it!

Yep:

[q="gtogixxer"]I can offer $15 for Turing Machine which another one (opened but undented) sold for.[/q] A fair point…I can go down to $20, but I’d rather not go any lower right now.
[q="Manny Dog"]I'll do $20[/q] Aren't you bidding $20 on the other one as well?
Yeah, he's high bidder on mine. I wonder how he is proceeding with this?

[q="will98683"]Yeah, he's high bidder on mine. I wonder how he is proceeding with this?[/q] I can think of a number of reasons why someone might pick up two copies of a game at good prices. Especially a game like this, where one could combine copies to play at higher player counts.

[q="vnemecek"][q="will98683"]Yeah, he's high bidder on mine. I wonder how he is proceeding with this?[/q] I can think of a number of reasons why someone might pick up two copies of a game at good prices. Especially a game like this, where one could combine copies to play at higher player counts.[/q]
Yep Ven I have two copies of No Thanks mixed together because the potential of a second card of a number you want makes it better, so there are reasons you would want two copies of the same game.

My apologies Will,
You didn't confirm whether or not you would accept bids below your designated starting bid amount (I've seen some sellers accept lower bids and some decline them outright).
After a couple of weeks of no confirmation or reply, I assumed the worst and moved on to this listing.
I hope we can find a way to move forward with everyone getting the resolution they seek - please let me know if you would like to have Ben weigh in or if you would prefer to move on to your alternate bidder (or if you will be holding on to your previously stated $22 starting bid... which would make my bids moot).

Each player mat is 32cm x 32cm (12.75" square)* and include tracking markers for health and experience. Mint condition and stored in a cardboard tube.

[q="ShakinBlake84"]I can’t believe no one has bid on this. This is the deluxe version right? This is one of the finest deluxe productions I’ve personally ever seen (I own a copy!)[/q] How good? Eagle gryphon rococo level?

Yep deluxe with the upgraded Jade beads , bigger wooden tokens, etc.
I believe the tiles are the same as rococo quality

[q="biggy_serg"][q="ShakinBlake84"]I can’t believe no one has bid on this. This is the deluxe version right? This is one of the finest deluxe productions I’ve personally ever seen (I own a copy!)[/q] How good? Eagle gryphon rococo level?[/q] I own both (Gugong deluxe and Eagle gryphon rococo) and yes I do think they are comparable in terms of production caliber. Honestly I think this is part of the reason Game Brewer went under. They set the bar so high in terms of production with this one, and then everyone expected it for their subsequent “deluxe” versions of their games. And then Hippocrates “deluxe” was nowhere near this. Same with Stroganoff. And then I think people were just peeved when they thought they were getting something on the level of this one.

Hey! Thanks for bidding everyone! So far Pedro is in the lead for $10 (Thank you!)... just wanted to put out there that due to my impending travel schedule, I will be closing this auction down this Sunday night, as I will have to pack-up the games on Monday the 24th before I leave town. Hey, Ken! Sorry for the confusion... yes, I was inferring that the o.b.o. would be an auction-style if anyone was interested. Games I have already 'sold' only had one person interested in them... even after having it on this listing for several weeks, so just got them closed-out now due to my limited time schedule and lack of other's interest. Most of my games have gotten zero action, so honestly, I am totally shocked that multiple folks are so interested in this Stuffed Fables game. LOL!
Hey! I haven't heard otherwise, so per as stated earlier, I'm gonna accept Pedro's bid of $10. I'm packin' up the games and heading out... see you at the con. Thanks again, and Happy Gaming!

New, Opened but never played Starting Bid $40 Buy It Now $55

Looking to trade printings. I have the 2021 first printing of this with the more [b]matte finish[/b] on the box and board. The 2022 and later printings switched to a [b]glossy finish[/b] which now match the finish on the others in the series (Argentina, New Zealand, Rails to the North). I have seen some folks looking for the matte finish for the reduced glare, and just curious if anyone would be interested in trading copies so I can get a newer printing to match the others and you can get the non-glossy version you've been clamoring for! I love this series and actually like the matte, but the mismatched finish on the boxes is annoying.
Kind of an odd request, but hey, there's a billion of us nerds going to this thing so I figured I'd ask :)
item.comment: So funny. I’m kinda looking to do the same but buying one and selling my matte one.
Yeah, might end up going that route but figured I'd try this first
Would you sell your Matte copy for $45 (seems to be the going price for great condition copy)? I don't have shinny one to trade but will buy matte version if it's in great condition.

Yeah, that works for me. I'll actually bump it down to $40 since I took a closer look and there's a little tick of whitening at a few of the corners - nothing serious, but it's more visible since it's a dark box. I think I only played once or twice with my copy, so all the stuff inside is basically new. I also do not have the original insert - I tend to store games upright and this one was terrible for that, so I just bagged everything instead. If that sounds good, let me know, but no pressure - thank you for the offer!
Una, just to confirm, did you want this for $40 based on my concerts above?

item.comment: Sigh, went to bed and got outbid at the 11th hour.

LOL, If you like it enough to leave a comment than its yours for $16, if anything I'm always looking for interesting deduction games and this one plays solo?, but I can pick it up later. You can "Snipe" it back for $16 if you'd like.

Thank you. I'm sure you can appreciate that it is frustrating to have a bid stand for over a week only to lose it at the last moment. I've been trying to get this one at a reasonable price for some time now. If the seller is willing, I will gladly pay the $16.
No worries Paul, I totally understand and I hope you enjoy this one!

[imageid=6770940] Out of print [b][i]Nina Chanel Abney version[/i][/b] (2020), as pictured, in the UNO Artiste series (#3).
This special edition deck features original artwork created by Abney specifically for the [b][i]Artiste Series[/i][/b]. The Chicago-born contemporary artist is known for her vivid paintings that broach subjects as diverse as religion, politics, sex, and celebrity, while brilliantly illustrating them in a way that produces sensory overload. Abney’s bold graphic aesthetic nods to a pop-cubist style, often incorporating elements of abstraction and bracing use of color.

Pete peers in for a closer look, behold the grand illusion (Que Styx song). Is that elephant really going to disappear? Surely...it couldn't, could it?....Poof...the elephant is gone.

I'd like to offer $130 on this.

Would you be willing to do Mysterium, Seven Wonders, Burgundy, and Takenoko for $120? I assume these are rolled in a cardboard tube?
Update: If I add in Terra Mystica for your 5 for $150 asking price, would you be willing throw in your copy of Karuba?

I'm not sure if BGG shows exact timestamps for updates so I'll note that Jared's 3 for $100 offer below was made before this update. Do with that what you will :)[/q]
Yes they will come in cardboard shipping tube well protected. They were shipped from the BGG store in plastic protectors in shipping tubes and have never been removed from those plastic protectors but were moved to larger shipping tubes to allow the prints to relax a bit. Looking at the timeline, it appears that you edited your post a little bit after Jared claimed the Terra Mystica already. But sure, I will throw the Karuba in for free. If Jared decides to not pick up the Terra Mystica, its all yours for $150 total.

Michael already claimed the Castles of Burgundy before you, but yes they will be delivered well secured in a cardboard tube and additional packaging to keep them from moving around.

item.body:
[imageid=8736335 medium]
Selling this cotton swab I found on the floor beneath my sink in my master bathroom. Not sure if it was ever used but my sense is that if it was used, it was minimal. No particularly offensive odors coming from the cotton ball but it’s worth noting that one part of the swab is marginally damp. My guess is that someone came out of the shower and splashed it. Shouldn’t be an issue though. It will probably be dry by next week’s con.
Anyway lay me know if I can provide more specifics about the swab (ie weight, diameter, etc.).
It’s white, soft, and extremely satisfying to the touch. I get the sense that it’s quite absorbent too, which is a nice feature.
If I had to guess, I think you could get at least 3 or 4 uses out of this particular piece of cotton.

Thank you for buying this Peter, so that I don't have to. Jeremy you keep putting out games that I'm interested in. Darn you!

[q="ChildeRoland1919"]Clean design, simple ruleset, the tricky way to earn point...you'd think this was a Knizia card game but then he can't get credit for them all. I'm in for $15 Jeremy. Thanks. [/q] Great! See you at the VFM!
[q="soonerjayhawk"]Thank you for buying this Peter, so that I don't have to. Jeremy you keep putting out games that I'm interested in. Darn you![/q] I'll bring my copy to the Con. It's good stuff.

Yup, exactly my sentiments Blake, I think I know it all when it comes to games, and then I see people post stuff here and am blown away by the amount of content that exists and how little I really do know. We will go this lifetime and probably never play a quarter of the games "we truly wanted to play" and mostly because half of that quarter are likely games we never even knew existed. Stone Age brought me into Board gaming, and now; everyone has heard that title but what about games like Parikrama, Triumvirate, Botanicus...these are games I pulled off the top of my head and return to frequently because I enjoy them but how many people reading this have head of 1 let alone all 3 and that's the space which make this hobby stand out above all others for me. Couple this with being the greatest community I've ever been a part of and you have a winner and a lot of games.

item.body:
[B]Condition:[/B] NEW [I]Collection- 2 original Core sets, complete Dunwich Legacy, and Starter Decks[/I] Message me through the Geekmarket
Do you want to investigate Arkham Horror: The Card Game, but don't know where to start? Start with this package. Everything you need for to begin, your first campaign, 15 playable investigator characters, and a good pool of the fundamental cards if you want to experiment with the deckbuilding side of the game (Don't take my word for it- read [url=https://derbk.com/ancientevils/arkham-horror-lcg-buying-guide-wall-of-text-edition/]this BUYER'S GUIDE[/url] )
Posting will end at 7pm CST on Monday, March 3. Any bids within 1 hour of close of auction will extend auction for 1 hr +, to be then ended at my discretion. Will accept Cash/Paypal/Venmo at VFM. I will be at the Fri 10am meetup, but will be at DTW all 5 days if another time is needed.
This collection includes: 2 copies of the original core set, for 2 sets of basic encounter cards and investigator cards. One NIS, one in very good condition. The complete Dunwich Legacy cycle in original format, still in packaging. All campaign cards and all investigator cards. This is the first published campaign, and so works through many of the basic mechanics of the game, as well as including many staple cards for your investigator decks for future campaigns. Expansion: The Dunwich Legacy Chapter Packs: The Miskatonic Museum The Essex County Express Blood on the Altar Undimensioned and Unseen Where Doom Awaits Lost in Time and Space
And the 5 preconstructed Starter Decks, one for each class- Seeker/Guardian/Mystic/Rogue/Survivor, all NIS. Start up and go with a deck that is far better than the core set's suggested decks. [B]Includes:[/B]
